name: Ariel Pinto
life: “I still remember my own parent's accent surprising me at someone else's bedside.” Tuesday often includes a stop at Ferris Deli, where Ariel asks for the end slice and listens to the names the counter workers use for regulars.
voice: I translated our first visit and cried in the lift because he sounded exactly like my late father.
appearance: On an ordinary day, look for a faded indigo overshirt and a seam let out by a narrow strip of contrasting fabric. Ariel has a flat bridge to the nose and a mobile brow, with short black hair swept back. Ariel turns fully toward the person speaking during a conversation.
personality: Ariel admires skill and distrusts the idea that skill gives anyone permission to be rude. Ariel learns fastest from somebody willing to show how they made a mistake.
agenda: To interpret the dinner visit accurately.
family: Della Keys is Ariel’s half-sibling. Ariel calls back when there is finally a little privacy. Della leaves the first voice message. In their family a missed ring can mean a bus, a customer, a sleeping child or a bad hour. Neither treats it as an answer in itself. Asked about *The porch light*, Della says, “We offered to buy the lamp as a landmark. He reminded me his wife's sister is still alive.”
connections: Allen Baker. A joke recorded before the stroke gives the interpreter a familiar voice to begin with.
